extracted.intended_audience: patent owners, patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), and third-party reexamination requesters
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive USPTO rules for conducting ex parte and inter partes reexamination and for requesting/processing supplemental examination of patents, including filing content, formatting, timelines, duties of disclosure, interviews, and certificates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes shown by markings
rubrics_metrics.description: Any changes relative to the patent being reexamined which are made to the specification, including the claims, must include the following markings: the matter to be omitted must be enclosed in brackets; the matter to be added must be underlined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to all specification and claim changes made during reexamination proceedings; ensures clarity of deletions and additions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering of patent claims preserved
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent claims may not be renumbered. The numbering of any claims added in the reexamination proceeding must follow the number of the highest numbered patent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New claims must continue numbering sequence from the existing highest claim number; renumbering is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of disclosure when required
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosure must be amended, when required by the Office, to correct inaccuracies of description and definition, and to secure substantial correspondence between the claims, the remainder of the specification, and the drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office may require specification/drawing amendments to ensure consistency with claims; such amendments are directed to correcting inaccuracies and securing substantial correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments must be relative to the patent as filed
rubrics_metrics.description: All amendments must be made relative to the patent specification, including the claims, and drawings, which are in effect as of the date of filing the request for reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments are judged against the patent document in effect on the request filing date—not against any later drafts.

rubrics_metrics.name: No enlargement of claim scope
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment may enlarge the scope of the claims of the patent or introduce new matter. No amendment may be proposed for entry in an expired patent. Moreover, no amendment, other than the cancellation of claims, will be incorporated into the patent by a certificate issued after the expiration of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments cannot broaden claim scope or add subject matter; time-limited restriction for expired patents—only cancellations permitted after expiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments effective only upon certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the Office actions will treat proposed amendments as though they have been entered, the proposed amendments will not be effective until the reexamination certificate is issued and published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed amendments have no legal effect until the reexamination certificate issues and is published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of inventorship in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: When it appears the correct inventor(s) were not named, the Director may, on petition of all parties set forth in § 1.324 and satisfactory proof and payment of fee § 1.20(b), include in the reexamination certificate an amendment naming only the actual inventor(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition must be submitted as part of the reexamination proceeding and satisfy § 1.324 requirements. If reexamination concludes other than by certificate, a certificate of correction may be issued upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply by third party requester in ex parte reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply to the patent owner’s statement under § 1.530 may be filed by the ex parte reexamination requester within two months from the date of service of the patent owner’s statement and must be served on the patent owner in accordance with § 1.248.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent owner does not file a statement under § 1.530, no reply or other submission from the ex parte requester will be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of responses in ex parte reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to timely file or serve the documents set forth in § 1.530 or § 1.535 may result in their being refused consideration. No submissions other than the statement pursuant to § 1.530 and the reply by the ex parte requester pursuant to § 1.535 will be considered prior to examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict adherence to the specified response types and deadlines is required for consideration prior to examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct of ex parte reexamination with special dispatch
rubrics_metrics.description: All ex parte reexamination proceedings, including any appeals to the Board, will be conducted with special dispatch within the Office; after order and expiration of time for responses, examination will follow §§ 1.104–1.116 and result in issuance of an ex parte reexamination certificate under § 1.570.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceedings are expedited; examination procedures mirror normal examination rules cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner response period for Office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner in an ex parte reexamination proceeding will be given at least thirty days to respond to any Office action. Responses may include further statements and/or proposed amendments or new claims to place the patent in a condition where all claims, if amended as proposed, would be patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimum 30-day response window; responses can include substantive amendments and arguments designed to achieve patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time for patent owner actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for extension must specify the requested period and be accompanied by the petition fee set forth in § 1.17(g). Third‑party-requested ex parte reexamination extension requests must be filed on or before the due date and are not granted absent sufficient cause or for more than a reasonable time. Patent-owner requested extensions up to two months must be filed no later than two months from expiration; longer extensions follow stricter filing timing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mere filing of a request does not effect extension; extensions limited by cause and statute; reply must be filed prior to expiration of extension period and never later than the statutory maximum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination for failure to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent owner fails to file a timely and appropriate response to any Office action or any written statement of an interview required under § 1.560(b), the prosecution in the ex parte reexamination proceeding will be a terminated prosecution, and the Director will proceed to issue and publish a certificate concluding the reexamination in accordance with the last action of the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to meet response obligations leads to terminated prosecution and issuance of certificate based on last Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to revive a terminated reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: If a response by the patent owner is not timely filed, a petition may be filed pursuant to § 1.137 to revive a reexamination prosecution terminated under paragraph (d) if the delay in response was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relief via petition requires showing unintentional delay and follows § 1.137 procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and consideration of Office actions/documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The reexamination requester will be sent copies of Office actions during the ex parte reexamination. After filing of a request by a third party requester, any document filed by either party must be served on the other party in the manner provided by § 1.248 and must reflect service or may be refused consideration by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service proof is required for documents to be considered; Office ensures both parties receive relevant correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: End of active participation by ex parte requester
rubrics_metrics.description: The active participation of the ex parte reexamination requester ends with the reply pursuant to § 1.535; no further submissions on behalf of the requester will be acknowledged unless in accordance with § 1.510 or § 1.535 or entered in the patent file prior to the date of the order for ex parte reexamination pursuant to § 1.525.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party participation in ex parte reexamination is strictly limited and time-bound.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party submissions after order
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions by third parties, filed after the date of the order for ex parte reexamination pursuant to § 1.525, must meet the requirements of and will be treated in accordance with § 1.501(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-order third-party input must follow the specified rule and format to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition fee requirement in ex parte proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition in an ex parte reexamination proceeding must be accompanied by the fee set forth in § 1.20(c)(6), except for specific petitions (e.g., certain extension petitions, acceptance of delayed responses, unintentionally delayed benefit claims, and correction of inventorship petitions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most petitions require payment; listed exceptions do not require the § 1.20(c)(6) fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of reexamination (evidence and statutory bases)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims in an ex parte reexamination will be examined on the basis of patents or printed publications and, with respect to subject matter added or deleted in the reexamination proceeding, on the basis of the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 112.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reexamination uses patents/printed publications as primary art sources; added/deleted subject matter is judged for compliance with 35 U.S.C.112 (written description/enablement/definiteness).

rubrics_metrics.name: No enlargement of claims in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims in an ex parte reexamination proceeding will not be permitted to enlarge the scope of the claims of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reexamination cannot be used to broaden claim scope; a substantive limitation on allowable amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited issues resolved in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Issues other than those indicated (patents/printed publications and 35 U.S.C.112 matters) will not be resolved in a reexamination proceeding. If such issues are raised, the examiner will note them as unresolved in the next Office action, and the patent owner may consider filing a reissue application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reexamination is narrow in scope; other substantive issues may be deferred to reissue or other proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of patent owner statements of record
rubrics_metrics.description: Any statement of the patent owner and any accompanying information submitted pursuant to § 1.501(a)(2) which is of record in the patent being reexamined may be used after a reexamination proceeding has been ordered to determine the proper meaning of a patent claim when applying patents or printed publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior statements of the patent owner (e.g., in file history) can be used as claim construction evidence in reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to disclose information material to patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: Each individual associated with the patent owner in a reexamination proceeding has a duty of candor and good faith to disclose to the Office all information known to that individual to be material to patentability in a reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Those with duty include the patent owner, each attorney/agent representing the owner, and every individual substantively involved on behalf of the owner. Duty exists for each claim pending until cancelled. Duty deemed satisfied if all material information was cited by Office or submitted in an IDS; fraud or intentional misconduct violates the duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and content requirements for IDS in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Any information disclosure statement must be filed with the items listed in § 1.98(a) as applied to individuals associated with the patent owner in a reexamination proceeding, should be filed within two months of the date of the order for reexamination, or as soon thereafter as possible, and be accompanied by any applicable IDS size fee under § 1.17(v).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IDS timing is prompt after order; size fees may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of material information in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Information is material when it is not cumulative and (1) it is a patent or printed publication that establishes, by itself or in combination, a prima facie case of unpatentability of a claim; or (2) it refutes or is inconsistent with a position the patent owner takes in opposing unpatentability relied on by the Office or asserting patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prima facie of unpatentability means information compels a conclusion of unpatentability under the preponderance standard, giving each term its broadest reasonable construction consistent with the specification, before considering contrary evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance responsibility and Office non-evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: The responsibility for compliance with the disclosure duties rests upon the designated individuals and no evaluation will be made by the Office in the reexamination proceeding as to compliance with this section. Questions of compliance raised will be noted as unresolved per § 1.552(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office does not proactively police compliance; disputes are recorded as unresolved issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview location and timing restrictions in ex parte reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews between examiners and patent owners (or their attorneys/agents) must be conducted in the Office during Office hours at times the examiner designates and will not be permitted at any other time or place without authority of the Director. Interviews for discussion of patentability of claims will not be conducted prior to the first official action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews must be arranged in advance; reexamination requesters cannot participate in interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written statement requirement for interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: In every instance of an interview with an examiner in an ex parte reexamination, a complete written statement of the reasons presented at the interview as warranting favorable action must be filed by the patent owner. The written statement does not remove the necessity for response to Office actions and must be filed as a separate part of a response to an outstanding Office action or as a separate paper within one month from the date of the interview, whichever is later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oral interview content must be memorialized in a separate written submission within the prescribed time; failure to do so does not eliminate the need to respond to Office actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to notify Office of concurrent proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: In an ex parte reexamination proceeding the patent owner must inform the Office of any prior or concurrent proceedings in which the patent is or was involved (e.g., interferences, reissues, reexaminations, litigation) and the results of such proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification helps the Office manage concurrent or related proceedings; see § 1.985 for inter partes specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director discretion on suspension/merger when litigation or concurrent files
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent in ex parte reexamination is or becomes involved in litigation, the Director shall determine whether to suspend the reexamination. If ex parte reexamination is ordered while a prior ex parte reexamination is pending and prosecution in the prior one has not been terminated, proceedings will usually be merged resulting in issuance of a single certificate. Similar merger/suspension rules apply for reissue applications and interferences under specified conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director has authority to suspend or merge based on overlap or pendency in other proceedings; procedures for merger include maintaining same claims during merged prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuance and publication of ex parte reexamination certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: To conclude an ex parte reexamination, the Director will issue and publish an ex parte reexamination certificate under 35 U.S.C. 307 setting forth the results and the content of the patent following the proceeding. The certificate will be mailed to the patent owner and a copy mailed to the requester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If certificate cancels all patent claims, no further Office proceedings will be conducted for that patent or related reissue/reexamination requests. Notices are published in the Official Gazette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental examination requestor eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for supplemental examination of a patent must be filed by the owner(s) of the entire right, title, and interest in the patent. Any party other than the patent owner is prohibited from filing papers or otherwise participating in any manner in a supplemental examination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the full patent owner can initiate supplemental examination; third parties may not participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for supplemental examination requests
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for supplemental examination of a patent may be filed at any time during the period of enforceability of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no statutory preclusion during enforceability period; multiple requests allowed over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on items of information in supplemental examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Each request for supplemental examination may include no more than twelve items of information believed to be relevant to the patent. More than one request for the same patent may be filed at any time during enforceability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count items individually; combining items in a request may cause each component to be separately counted except certain enumerated exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and form of an item of information
rubrics_metrics.description: An item of information includes a document submitted as part of the request that contains information the patent owner requests the Office to consider, reconsider, or correct. If the information is not contained within or based on any submitted document, the discussion within the body of the request relative to the information will be considered an item. An item must be in writing; audio/video must be submitted as a written transcript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-document discussions count as items; non written media must be transcribed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions for combined items counting
rubrics_metrics.description: If one item is combined with additional items, each may be separately counted. Exceptions include combining a non-English document and its translation, and combining a document over 50 pages with its summary pursuant to § 1.610(b)(8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translations and long-document summaries are not separately counted as multiple items in those specific combinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and fee requirements for supplemental examination request
rubrics_metrics.description: A request must be accompanied by filing fee (§ 1.20(k)(1)), fee for reexamination ordered as a result (§ 1.20(k)(2)), and document size fees (§ 1.20(k)(3)). It must include patent number, a list of items of information (meeting § 1.98(b) where appropriate), identification of other prior/concurrent post-patent Office proceedings, identification of each claim for which supplemental examination is requested, a separate detailed explanation of the relevance and manner of applying each item to each identified claim, a copy of the patent and any disclaimers/certificates, copies of each item with written English translation of necessary parts of non-English items, summaries for documents over 50 pages, and identification of owner(s) with proof of entirety of ownership per § 3.73(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request must be complete and accompanied by required fees; incomplete requests risk not receiving a filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office will refuse filing date for noncompliant supplemental requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date will not be granted if the request is not in compliance with §§ 1.605, 1.615, and § 1.610, subject to Office discretion. The Office will notify the patent owner and provide an opportunity to complete the request within a specified time; failure to timely comply results in no filing date and refund of the reexamination fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely correctable defects can be fixed to obtain filing date; if corrected timely the filing date is the receipt date of the corrected request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format requirements for supplemental examination papers
rubrics_metrics.description: All papers submitted in a supplemental examination must be formatted in accordance with § 1.52. Court documents and non-patent literature may be redacted but must otherwise be identical in content and format to the original documents and must not be reduced in size or modified in font, spacing, or margins. Patents, patent application publications, and third-party-generated affidavits or declarations must not be reduced in size or otherwise modified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintaining original format and legibility is required; redactions allowed but format must otherwise match originals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required components and organizational attachments for request
rubrics_metrics.description: The request should include a cover sheet itemizing each component submitted, a table of contents, an explanation of how the claims patentably distinguish over the items of information, and an explanation of why each item does or does not raise a substantial new question of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These organizational elements facilitate Office review and are expected per § 1.615.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office determination on substantial new question (SNQ)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within three months after the filing date of a request, the Office will determine whether a substantial new question of patentability affecting any claim is raised by any of the items presented. The determination will generally be limited to a review of the item(s) identified in the request as applied to the identified claim(s) and will be based on the claims in effect at the time of the determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SNQ review is targeted and time-limited; determination becomes part of the official patent record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative handling during supplemental examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may hold in abeyance action on any petition or other paper until after the proceeding is concluded; unauthorized or improper papers will not be entered or will be expunged. The patent owner must promptly notify the Office of discovery of any other prior or concurrent post-patent Office proceeding limited to identifying that proceeding (no discussion). Interviews are prohibited and no amendments may be filed in the supplemental examination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental examination is documentary and non-adversarial: no interviews or amendments; procedural housekeeping rules apply to keep record clean.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral to U.S. Attorney General on suspected material fraud
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Office becomes aware during supplemental examination or any reexamination ordered as a result that a material fraud on the Office may have been committed in connection with the patent, the proceeding will continue and the matter will be referred to the U.S. Attorney General in accordance with 35 U.S.C. 257(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental examination does not immunize suspected fraud; fraud triggers referral to enforcement authorities and continuation of proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusion and possible outcomes of supplemental examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplemental examination concludes with electronic issuance of a supplemental examination certificate indicating whether any of the items raised a substantial new question of patentability. If SNQ is raised, ex parte reexamination will be ordered under 35 U.S.C. 257 and an ex parte reexamination certificate will be published upon conclusion. If no SNQ is raised and reexamination is not ordered, the certificate will be published and the fee for reexamination (if collected) will be refunded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificate becomes public record. If reexamination is ordered from supplemental exam, the ensuing reexamination follows §§ 1.530–1.570 with specified exceptions (e.g., patent owner will not have the right to file a statement under § 1.530; reexamination may be based on any item in § 1.605; issues beyond patents/printed publications may be considered; information material to patentability defined by § 1.56(b)).
